selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What everyday blessing does the passage use to teach a lesson about Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: It uses milk produced in animals and human mothers.

questions.question: Where is this milk formed according to the passage?
questions.answer: It is produced inside the body in a place surrounded by blood and waste.

questions.question: What special qualities of milk are mentioned?
questions.answer: It is pure, clean, pleasant, nourishing, and white.

questions.question: Besides milk, what other gift to the young is described in the passage?
questions.answer: Mothers are given deep kindness and care for their babies.

questions.question: How does that motherly care compare with milk in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as even sweeter and more precious.

questions.question: Which qualities of Allah are shown by giving both milk and mercy to mothers?
questions.answer: His mercy, wisdom, knowledge, power, will, and careful care are shown.

questions.question: Why does the passage say chance and blind forces cannot be the cause of this?
questions.answer: Because something so wise, pure, caring, and well-arranged cannot come from random or mindless causes.

questions.question: How wide is the spread of this sign in creation?
questions.answer: It appears across the whole earth in countless mothers from many kinds of creatures.

questions.question: What detail shows that this work is unified and controlled by one Lord?
questions.answer: It happens at the same time and in the same orderly way with the same wisdom and care.

questions.question: What main conclusion does the passage draw from this example?
questions.answer: It is a clear proof that Allah is One.

questions.question: What is the main message of the verse about cattle in this passage?
questions.answer: It teaches people to learn from how Allah provides pure milk from living bodies.

questions.question: Which creatures are directly named as giving milk in the passage?
questions.answer: Cows, camels, goats, sheep, and human mothers.

questions.question: What contrast in the body makes the production of milk especially amazing?
questions.answer: Milk comes out pure and wholesome even though it is formed between things that are dirty and red with blood.

questions.question: What does this contrast help the reader understand about the Creator?
questions.answer: It shows that the Creator works with perfect wisdom and control.

questions.question: What feeling is placed in mothers’ hearts?
questions.answer: Love and tenderness for their young.

questions.question: Why is this tenderness an important part of the argument in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that feeding the young is not only physical but also guided by mercy and care.

questions.question: What false explanations are rejected in this section?
questions.answer: Random chance, mixed-up elements, and blind forces are rejected.

questions.question: What reason is given for rejecting those explanations?
questions.answer: They cannot produce such careful, wise, and purposeful results.

questions.question: How does the passage use the repeated pattern among many mothers to support its point?
questions.answer: The same beautiful work appearing everywhere shows one Maker is behind it all.

questions.question: If an 8th grader had to state the lesson of this passage in one sentence, what would it be?
questions.answer: The pure milk and loving care given to countless mothers are clear signs that one wise and merciful Allah creates and manages all things.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can people learn by thinking about milk?
questions.answer: They can learn about Allah’s unity and His careful mercy.

questions.question: Why is milk described as the opposite of what surrounds it inside the body?
questions.answer: Because it comes out clean and beneficial even though it is produced near impure substances.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the process that produces milk?
questions.answer: It is controlled with exact wisdom and cannot be accidental.

questions.question: What human example is included along with grazing animals?
questions.answer: Human mothers are also mentioned.
